correctness.rationale: Derived E(t) from K²=κ²I, verified each trace-term expansion with cyclicity and P1P2=0, and verified determinant conservation. Strictly positive monodromy gives two distinct positive eigenvalues; fixed-determinant Perron root is strictly trace-increasing. The cosh-product identity establishes global phase uniqueness. For Δ<1 the eigenvalue threshold equals H=1+Δ. An exact rational example shows opposite threshold signs, checked independently in check.py. The standalone program passed 9,005 checks; finite sampling is supporting only.

evidence: The general Floquet analysis of Georgescu et al. computes the multiplier for a simultaneous treatment regime and a time-dependent two-patch SI system, not an exact all-offset ordering of two distinct diagonal impulses.
Terry (2010) proves sufficient pulse-eradication conditions for a structured delay equation but does not compare every continuous phase in the claimed constant two-compartment setting.

Byers & Castle (2005), J Econ Entomol 98:1763–1773, https://academic.oup.com/jee/article-abstract/98/6/1763/2218357, abstract reports simulation-based synchrony advantages under threshold-triggered grid-wide sprays.

Browne et al., arXiv:1309.0265 (first posted 2013), journal 2015, §6.1 Theorem 5 establishes a local synchrony optimum only for identical patches with no infected movement/cross-transmission; Figure 6 numerically illustrates extinction at synchronous and persistence at offset vaccinations in the SIR model, and §7 states the broader analytic synchrony question remains open for their model.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general ecological point that synchronous control can help is explicitly known, and is not claimed novel. Existing qualitative simulation results and sufficient conditions are weaker in a distinct direction from the exact spectral-radius phase ordering for every asymmetric two-state constant generator and fixed cull rates. A general positive-matrix rearrangement theorem potentially subsuming the exact law was not identified; historical coverage remains provisional. Browne et al. establishes a closely analogous local and numerical timing effect, but it is not stronger coverage of a 2x2 Metzler direct-cull product and supplies neither the exact global all-phase trace formula nor strict half-period maximum for arbitrary unequal parameters.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A direct special case of an extant theorem would be covered even without matching words. The inspected source theorems neither supply a universal offset parameter nor quantify its strict half-period spectral ordering, so no direct implication was found. Since plausible full texts and more general matrix-rearrangement results remain unverified, priority is assessed within inspected literature, not asserted universally. The nearest proved prior timing theorem for coupled regional vaccination has a different pulsed state variable, a different epidemic reproduction operator, and assumptions excluding infected movement; the new claim does not follow as a corollary or special case.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Checked the most direct positive-matrix/Floquet representation as well as epidemiological and pest-control synonyms. Simultaneous two-patch spraying has no variable phase, so no implication of a strictly increasing half-period defect. Terry permits independent schedules but the inspected proof supplies eradication bounds rather than the claimed universal spectral trace identity; it is not demonstrably equivalent or dominating. The particularly relevant Browne et al. 2014 Theorem 5 is not a direct reduction: vaccination acts on susceptibles with replenishment, while the proposed claim concerns fixed direct multiplicative culls of the two linear growth coordinates, with nonzero between-patch migration; their theorem is only local at phase zero under symmetric restrictions.

value.rationale: The phase ordering is a motivated sharp quantitative answer to a two-farm pest-control coordination problem in established pre-2016 literature: exactly when equal-frequency and equal-strength regional interventions cross an eradication boundary merely by timing. It accommodates asymmetric migration and unequal growth/cull efficacy and gives a reproducible exact stability reversal. No inference about nonlinear full dynamics or practical pesticide optimality is made.
